dedupe_keys.name: ewatercycle platform for running and comparing hydrological models

description: eWaterCycle is an open Python platform that makes it easier to run, compare and couple hydrological models written in different languages, so that modellers can work together on large-scale and local hydrology for floods, droughts and land use change. It covers a common interface to models that are packaged as plugins and run in containers through the Basic Model Interface with grpc4bmi or remotebmi, forcing generation with ESMValTool, and comparison against observations from GRDC or USGS; the package ships without models, which are installed as endorsed plugins. It is developed by the eWaterCycle team, with blog posts from 2018 to 2022 describing the project, and the ewatercycle Python package reached version 2.6.0 on 16 September 2026. The package is available from PyPI and GitHub under the Apache 2.0 licence, free of charge, with documentation on Read the Docs. Caveats: running models needs container support and downloaded forcing data. It supports reproducible hydrological modelling for flood and drought hazard analysis of water and green-blue infrastructure and climate adaptation; a related record is the OGC OpenMI standard.
